# @actdim/msgmesh-store - Full Documentation Context

> **Decoupled Message Bus Bridge & Change Data Capture (CDC) Engine Connecting @actdim/msgmesh with Persistent Stores (LiveStruct & LiveStore)**

---

## Document: README.md (Overview)

# @actdim/msgmesh-store

> **Decoupled Message Bus Bridge & Change Data Capture (CDC) Engine Connecting @actdim/msgmesh with Persistent Stores (LiveStruct & LiveStore)**

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@actdim/msgmesh-store.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@actdim/msgmesh-store)
[![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-5.9+-blue.svg)](https://www.typescriptlang.org/)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-green.svg)](LICENSE)

---

## 1. What is MsgMesh-Store?

**`@actdim/msgmesh-store`** is the architectural bridge between in-memory message buses (`@actdim/msgmesh`) and local-first persistent stores (`@actdim/livestruct` and `@livestore/livestore`).

### Why is this Integration Needed?

If LiveStore already synchronizes state across browser tabs via SQLite and `BroadcastChannel`, why introduce a message bus?

**LiveStore solves storage, not communication.** A message bus is required whenever interactions cross execution boundaries or involve non-persistent orchestration:

1. **Web Worker Boundary Crossing:**
   Running SQLite WASM and heavy computational solvers in a Web Worker means the main UI thread cannot hold direct in-memory reactive object proxies. `@actdim/msgmesh-store` bridges commands and change deltas across the `postMessage` boundary with zero proxy serialization overhead.
2. **Change Data Capture (CDC) for Decoupled Services:**
   Decoupled modules (audit logs, analytics, minimaps, cloud sync watermarks) need to react when database records change, without holding direct class instances or query subscriptions to the underlying documents.
3. **Command Bus (CQRS Pipeline):**
   UI toolbars emit domain intents (`cad.command.extrude_face`) rather than mutating database tables directly. The store bridge normalizes and validates command payloads (`STORE.COMMAND`) and serializes them per document before committing to storage; domain-level validation stays in your own bus handlers.
4. **Echo Suppression (Feedback Loop Protection):**
   When a document change emits a bus event and a bus listener triggers a patch, an infinite loop can easily form. The bridge includes built-in origin tracking (`local`, `remote`, `bus`) and a deterministic, count-bounded mutation ledger: changes applied from bus commands are never republished to the bus.

---

## 2. When to Use (and When NOT to Use)

| Scenario | Recommended Approach | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Local UI Form in the same thread | **Direct In-Memory Mutation (LiveDocument / Model)** | Direct property access is faster, fully type-safe, and avoids serialized bus hops. |
| UI thread to Web Worker storage | **@actdim/msgmesh-store Bridge** | Serialized delta packets carry data across threads cleanly. |
| Decoupled services (audit, sync) | **Store CDC Events via Bus** | Modules listen to `STORE.ENTITY_CHANGED` without tight coupling to models. |
| High-frequency interactions (60fps drag) | **Pure In-Memory MsgMesh** | Transient events bypass the disk log entirely. |

---

## 3. Quick Code Example

```typescript
import { createMsgBus } from '@actdim/msgmesh/core';
import { attachStoreBridge } from '@actdim/msgmesh-store';
import { createLiveStruct } from '@actdim/livestruct';
import type { StoreCdcEvent } from '@actdim/msgmesh-store/cdc';

// 1. Instantiate bus and store
const bus = createMsgBus();
const store = await createLiveStruct({ name: 'workspace_db' });
const parts = await store.collection('parts');

// 2. Attach store bridge to bus (defaults to channelPrefix: 'STORE')
const bridge = attachStoreBridge(bus, parts, {
    enableCdcStream: true,
    enableCommandHandling: true,
});

// 3. Decoupled services listen to change events via the message bus
bus.on({
    channel: 'STORE.ENTITY_CHANGED',
    group: 'out',
    topic: 'parts',
    callback: (msg) => {
        const event = msg.payload as StoreCdcEvent;
        console.log('Entity changed:', event.type, event.id, event.delta);
    },
});

// 4. Remote module or worker dispatches command over the bus
await bus.send({
    channel: 'STORE.COMMAND',
    group: 'in',
    topic: 'parts',
    payload: { type: 'PATCH', id: 'part-101', delta: { color: 'green' } },
});
```

> **Note on Local In-Process Streams**: Local code in the same process can also subscribe directly to `bridge.cdc$` (or use the `subscribeCdc(bus)` helper) to receive an RxJS `Observable<StoreCdcEvent>` without manual message bus unpacking.

---

## 4. Architecture Overview

```text
  [ Local Forms / Dynstruct UI ]         [ Decoupled Services / Minimap / Cloud ]
                |                                          |
       Direct Model Mutation                       Listen to Bus Channels
                v                                          v
   +-------------------------+                     +---------------+
   |       LiveStruct        |                     |    MsgMesh    |
   | (High-Level Documents)  |                     |  (Message Bus)|
   +-------------------------+                     +---------------+
                |                                          ^
                | 1. Commit Mutation                       | 2. Stream CDC Deltas
                v                                          |
   +---------------------------------------------------------------+
   |                      @actdim/msgmesh-store                    |
   | (Bridge: Command Handling, Worker Boundary & Echo Suppression)|
   +---------------------------------------------------------------+
                                   |
                                   v
                         [ LiveStore / SQLite ]
```

---

## 5. Installation

```bash
pnpm add @actdim/msgmesh-store @actdim/msgmesh @actdim/livestruct @actdim/utico rxjs
```

`@actdim/livestruct` is an optional peer: any object matching the `StoreTarget` interface can be used instead.

# ALONG-PROTOCOL v4.6.0

This repo carries its own agent context, provider-agnostically. Follow it every session, whatever tool you are. This is the core; procedures (completion checklist, doc routing, merges, along-team, tool-use rules) live in `docs/topic--along-protocol.md` - pull the section you need via `/along-kb-search`. A gate's error message carries its detail.

## Where state lives
- **Nearest wins**: any folder may carry its own `AGENTS.md` + `.along/`; use the NEAREST for the area you work in. Nearest `.along/` > higher-level `.along/` > global config. Only a nested `.git` or a user-run `along init` makes a subproject.
- **Read at session start** (not auto-loaded): `.along/ISSUES.md`, `.along/CONSTRAINTS.md`, your issue `.along/ISSUES/<type>--<slug>.md`; when relevant `.along/VISION.md`, `.along/GLOSSARY.md`. They reflect the state WHEN WRITTEN - verify named files/APIs/flags against the code.
- **Entities**: issues (`feat|bug|debt|task|docs|spike`), ADRs (`.along/DECISIONS/`, never edited - superseded), milestones, sessions. Keys `<type>--<slug>`, referenced by key, never by path; schemas in `docs/topic--domain-model.md`. Create them from intent unprompted (build/fix -> issue, blocked -> issue tagged `risk`, compare -> `spike` issue, release -> milestone).
- **Projections** (`ISSUES.md`, `DECISIONS.md`, `CONSTRAINTS.md`, `docs/INDEX.md`) are compiled: on conflict take either side and re-run the sync.

## Anchor work to an issue
1. Find or create the issue with `status: in-progress`; `along start <slug>` binds this session.
2. Source edits unlock after the user approves the plan (`EnterPlanMode` -> `ExitPlanMode`, or `along plan approve --plan-file <path>` after their explicit yes). Questions get read-only answers; 1-line typo/comment edits are exempt.
3. Commit via `/along-commit`: bound to the slug, no AI `Co-Authored-By:` trailers.
4. Finish with the completion checklist, ending in `along wrap <slug> --summary "..." (--decisions <ADR...> | --no-decisions)`.

## Gates
Runtime hooks enforce these where installed; elsewhere (`along doctor` shows the level) self-apply every one and use the `along` CLI instead of raw tools.
- [gate: require-active-issue] [gate: require-plan-approval] - no source edit without an in-progress issue and an approved plan.
- [gate: subproject-boundary] - a subproject's entities go in ITS `.along/`; cross-subproject work needs an issue in each, or a root umbrella with `parent:` children.
- [gate: workspace-containment] - read/write inside the workspace (plus temp); other roots need `allowed_roots`; never credential stores.
- [gate: projection-protection] - never hand-edit or hand-merge projections.
- [gate: commit-issue-binding] - every commit names the active issue.
- [gate: issue-lifecycle] [gate: entity-reference-integrity] [gate: entity-deletion-protection] - close via `along wrap` / `along issue done`; rename or supersede, never delete a referenced entity.
- [gate: doc-manual-lock] - `write_policy: manual` docs change only under a `docs--<slug>` issue.
- [gate: rule-pack-protection] - never edit `.along/rules/**/*.md` (`along rules attach` owns them).
- [gate: doc-routing-compliance] - ADR vs `README.md` vs `docs/topic--*.md` routing tree.
- [gate: untracked-exports] - dashboards and `.along/diagnostics/` stay out of Git.
- [gate: cli_safety] - file content via file tools, never heredocs or `python -c`; no global installs.
- [gate: team-step-active] [gate: team-reviews-before-stop] - an `along-team` blackboard holds you to its step loop.
- [gate: test_before_stop] [gate: wrap_before_stop] [gate: projection_sync_before_stop] - before stopping: tests green, session wrapped, projections synced.
- [gate: unresolved_gate_denial] - a denied tool call is redone within the gate's rules or told to the user (`along gates ack`), never dropped silently; closing waits for their reply.
- Commit-time (`along lint`, pre-commit + CI): ASCII typography, fence languages, relative links, no `docs/` -> `.along/` links, Windows-safe names, no secrets, no stubs.
- Bypass is the user's call: `-n`, `--force-reason`, `scratch fallback` need `--reason` after their reply; recorded in `along gates stats`.

## Judgment rules
- Ground facts in code, `README.md` and `docs/`; no generic placeholders. Query `/along-kb-search` before reading whole docs; update affected `docs/topic--*.md` after non-trivial changes.
- Use `/along-test`, `/along-build`, `/along-dev` before raw commands, with quiet flags. Review your diff and blast radius (`along graph-impact`).
- Never delete or truncate docs, comments or code unless told; no stubs; check `git diff --stat` after batch edits. Verify written files parse. Tests stay hermetic.
- Scope > 3 files, crossing subsystems or refactoring core engines: route to `along-team`; plans MUST declare `Execution Mode: Direct` or `Role-Based`.
- Treat the `along` CLI as a black box (`along <cmd> --help`, no engine source outside the Along repo); report its errors verbatim.

## Project specifics

<!-- BEGIN ALONG-RULES -->
See the following engineering guidelines:
- `[languages/typescript.md](.along/rules/languages/typescript.md)`
- `[platforms/web.md](.along/rules/platforms/web.md)`
<!-- END ALONG-RULES -->

- **Package**: `@actdim/msgmesh-store` - bridge between the `@actdim/msgmesh` bus and persistent stores (LiveStruct / LiveStore): store bridge for command channels (`<prefix>.COMMAND`), CDC publishing (`<prefix>.ENTITY_CHANGED`), ledger-based echo suppression (`MutationLedger`), per-entity ordering (`KeyedSerialQueue`), and a worker transport (`attachWorkerStoreHost` / worker client).
- **Entry points**: `.` (`src/index.ts`), `./cdc`, `./bridge`, `./worker`. ESM only. Peers: `@actdim/msgmesh`, `@actdim/utico`, `rxjs`, optional `@actdim/livestruct`; runtime imports only `rxjs`, the rest is structural typing.
- **Commands** (package folder): `pnpm run build`, `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run test` (Vitest node), `pnpm run docs:build` (VitePress, published to https://actdim.github.io/msgmesh-store/ by `.github/workflows/pages.yml`).
- **Knowledge Base**: `docs/INDEX.md`; regenerate `docs/INDEX.md`, `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` with `along kb-sync <absolute package path>` after doc changes.
- **Versioning**: submodule of the mempart pnpm monorepo under one unified version; never bump `package.json` here in isolation (mempart `pnpm run version:sync <version>` only).

## Document: docs/topic--01-overview-and-advantages.md (Overview & Key Advantages)

# Overview & Key Advantages

[<- Back to README](../README.md) | [Next: 02. Core Concepts ->](./topic--02-core-concepts.md)

---

## What is @actdim/msgmesh-store?

**`@actdim/msgmesh-store`** is a small TypeScript library that connects a typed message bus (`@actdim/msgmesh`) with a document store (`@actdim/livestruct` or any structurally compatible engine). It provides three building blocks:

- **Store bridge** (`attachStoreBridge`) - listens for mutation commands on bus channels, applies them to the store, and republishes the resulting store changes as normalized Change Data Capture (CDC) events, without feeding its own writes back into the bus.
- **CDC stream** (`toStoreCdcObservable`, `createCdcBridge`, `publishCdcToBus`, `subscribeCdc`, `filterCdc`) - turns any engine, collection or observable into an RxJS stream of frozen `StoreCdcEvent` records and optionally publishes them on `<prefix>.ENTITY_CHANGED`.
- **Worker transport** (`createWorkerStoreClient`, `attachWorkerStoreHost`) - runs the store inside a Web Worker (or behind any `postMessage` port) and exposes a promise-based client on the main thread with request timeouts, lifecycle states, optional batching and a refcounted CDC stream.

The library imports only `rxjs` at runtime. The bus, the store and the port are all accepted through structural interfaces (`MsgMeshBusLike`, `StoreTarget`, `WorkerMessagePortLike`), so tests can pass plain objects and production code can pass a real `createMsgBus()` bus and a `createLiveStruct()` store.

---

## Why is this Integration Needed?

A local-first store already handles persistence and, with LiveStruct, cross-tab synchronization. It does not handle *communication*. A bus is needed when interactions cross execution or module boundaries:

1. **Worker boundary crossing.** When SQLite and heavy computation run in a Web Worker, the UI thread cannot hold the live document proxies. The worker transport serializes commands (`CREATE`, `PATCH`, `PATCH_PATH`, `DELETE`), raw SQL queries and CDC deltas across `postMessage` using the structured clone algorithm.
2. **CDC for decoupled services.** Audit logs, analytics, minimaps and sync watermarks want to know that a record changed without importing the collection or holding a query subscription. They subscribe to `STORE.ENTITY_CHANGED` (or a filtered `subscribeCdc(...)` stream) instead.
3. **Command bus.** UI code can emit store intents on `STORE.COMMAND` instead of calling the store directly. The bridge normalizes the payload, serializes writes per document and reports failures on `errors$`.
4. **Feedback loop protection.** When a store change is published on the bus and a bus listener writes back to the store, a loop forms easily. The bridge tracks every bus-applied mutation in a bounded `MutationLedger`, so changes that originated from the bus are never republished to it.

---

## When to Use (and When NOT to Use)

| Scenario | Recommended approach | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Local UI form in the same thread | Direct LiveStruct document access | Direct property access is faster, fully typed and avoids string channels. |
| UI thread to a store hosted in a Web Worker | `createWorkerStoreClient` + `attachWorkerStoreHost` | Typed request/response protocol with timeouts and a CDC stream. |
| Decoupled services (audit, analytics, sync) | `attachStoreBridge` or `createCdcBridge` + `subscribeCdc` | Consumers listen to `STORE.ENTITY_CHANGED` without coupling to models. |
| Remote or cross-module writers | `attachStoreBridge` command channels | Commands are validated, serialized per document and deduplicated by `mutationId`. |
| High-frequency transient interactions (60 fps drag) | Plain in-memory `@actdim/msgmesh` messages | Transient events do not need to touch the store at all. |

---

## Key Advantages

### 1. Deterministic echo suppression
- Every command applied through the bridge is recorded in a count-bounded `MutationLedger` (default capacity 4096).
- CDC events whose `mutationId` is in the ledger are emitted on the local `cdc$` stream but never republished to the bus.
- No time windows or debounce timers are involved; the old time-based `EchoTracker` is kept only for backwards compatibility and is deprecated.

### 2. Per-document ordering without global locks
- `KeyedSerialQueue` serializes commands per `collection:id` key in arrival order while unrelated documents execute concurrently.
- A failed command never blocks later commands for the same key.
- `whenIdle()` resolves when every queued command has settled - convenient in tests and shutdown paths.

### 3. One mutation semantics everywhere
- Both the bridge and the worker host call the same `applyStoreCommand` function, so `CREATE`, `PATCH`, `PATCH_PATH` and `DELETE` behave identically on the bus and across the worker boundary.
- `resolveMutationTarget` adapts a LiveStruct store instance, a low-level engine, a single collection or a custom object into one `MutationTarget` interface using only public members.

### 4. Safe, immutable CDC events
- CDC deltas are cloned and deep-frozen by default (`freezeEvents`), so a subscriber cannot corrupt store state or another subscriber's view.
- Malformed source items are dropped (and reported through `onInvalid`) without terminating the stream.
- `bus.send` failures are caught by `safeSend` and routed to `errors$` instead of becoming unhandled rejections.

### 5. Explicit worker lifecycle
- Client state is one of `idle`, `initializing`, `ready`, `dead`, `disposed`; calls on a dead or disposed client fail immediately with `WorkerDeadError`.
- Pending requests are rejected on timeout, on a `CLOSE` message, on a port `close` event or on a fatal `error` event.
- `reconnect(port?)` resets a dead client and re-establishes the handshake (and CDC subscription) on the same or a new port.

### 6. Hermetic testing
- `createMessageChannelPair()` returns two connected `InMemoryMessagePort` instances that behave like asynchronous `postMessage` ports, so the full worker protocol runs in Node without DOM globals.
- Every public entry point accepts structural types, so a mock bus is just an object with `send` and `on`.

---

| Import path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `@actdim/msgmesh-store` | Everything below plus the shared `core` module (`MutationLedger`, `KeyedSerialQueue`, `applyStoreCommand`, targets). |

| `@actdim/msgmesh-store/cdc` | CDC types and stream helpers. |
| `@actdim/msgmesh-store/worker` | Worker client, host, wire types and in-memory channel. |

## Document: docs/topic--02-core-concepts.md (Core Concepts)

# Core Concepts

[<- Back to 01. Overview & Advantages](./topic--01-overview-and-advantages.md) | [Next: 03. Architecture & Wiring ->](./topic--03-architecture-and-wiring.md)

---

This page explains each building block on its own. How they are combined is covered in [03. Architecture & Wiring](./topic--03-architecture-and-wiring.md); exact signatures are in [05. API Reference](./topic--05-api-reference.md).

## 1. CDC Events (`StoreCdcEvent`)

Every store change is normalized into one immutable record:

```typescript
interface StoreCdcEvent<T = Record<string, unknown>> {
    readonly type: 'insert' | 'update' | 'delete'; // StoreCdcType
    readonly collection: string;
    readonly id: string;
    readonly delta: Partial<T>;
    readonly origin: 'local' | 'remote' | 'bus'; // StoreCdcOrigin
    readonly timestamp: number;
    readonly mutationId?: string;
    readonly sourceId?: string;
}
```

- **`origin`** says where the change came from: `local` (direct store or engine write), `remote` (replication / sync), `bus` (applied from a bus command).
- **`mutationId`** identifies the write. The bridge uses it for echo suppression and deduplication.
- **`sourceId`** is stamped by a store bridge on the events it publishes to the bus (see section 3).

### Normalizing a source: `toStoreCdcObservable`

`toStoreCdcObservable(source, options)` accepts many shapes and returns an `Observable<StoreCdcEvent>`:

| Source shape | How the stream is found |
|---|---|
| An RxJS `Observable` | Used directly. |
| Object with `engine` (LiveStruct store instance) | Recurses into `source.engine`. |
| Object with `tableName` and `cdc$` (engine access) | Uses `cdc$`; collection defaults to `tableName`. |
| Object with `name` (collection) | Uses `cdc$`, `engineAccess.cdc$` or `engine.cdc$`; collection defaults to `name`. |
| Object with an observable `cdc$` | Uses `cdc$`. |
| Object with `cdcSubject.asObservable()` | Uses that observable. |

For each raw item it maps `type` (unknown values become `update`), resolves `collection` (item, inferred, `defaultCollection`, then `'default'`), reads `delta` or `data`, falls back to `defaultOrigin` (default `local`) and `Date.now()`. Non-object items are passed to `onInvalid` and dropped - the stream keeps running. When `freezeEvents` is not `false`, the delta is cloned (`safeClone`) and the event is deep-frozen (`deepFreeze`).

```typescript
import { Subject } from 'rxjs';
import { toStoreCdcObservable } from '@actdim/msgmesh-store/cdc';

const raw$ = new Subject<unknown>();
const cdc$ = toStoreCdcObservable(raw$, {
    defaultCollection: 'users',
    onInvalid: (err, item) => console.warn('dropped CDC item', item, err),
});

cdc$.subscribe((e) => console.log(e.type, e.collection, e.id, e.delta));
raw$.next({ type: 'insert', id: 'u-1', delta: { name: 'Alice' } });
```

### Filtering: `filterCdc`, `filterCollection`, `filterEntity`

RxJS operators over `StoreCdcEvent` streams:

```typescript
import { filterCdc, filterCollection, filterEntity } from '@actdim/msgmesh-store/cdc';

cdc$.pipe(filterCollection('orders'));
cdc$.pipe(filterEntity('orders', 'ord-42'));
cdc$.pipe(filterCdc({ collection: 'orders', originFilter: ['remote'], typeFilter: ['delete'] }));
```

Empty `originFilter` / `typeFilter` arrays mean "no filter".

## 2. CDC Bridge (`createCdcBridge`)

A CDC bridge is a one-way, disposable connection from a store source to an optional bus. It is the right tool when you only need to *publish* store changes and do not accept bus commands.

```typescript
import { createMsgBus } from '@actdim/msgmesh/core';
import { createLiveEngine } from '@actdim/livestruct';
import { createCdcBridge, subscribeCdc } from '@actdim/msgmesh-store/cdc';

const bus = createMsgBus();
const engine = await createLiveEngine({ name: 'app_db', forceMemory: true });

const cdc = createCdcBridge(engine, bus, { channelPrefix: 'STORE' });

subscribeCdc(bus, { channelPrefix: 'STORE', collection: 'accounts' })
    .subscribe((e) => console.log('account changed', e.id, e.delta));

await engine.insertDoc('accounts', 'acc-1', { balance: 10 });
cdc.dispose();
```

- Events are published on `<prefix>.ENTITY_CHANGED` (group `out`, topic = collection). With `secondaryChannelPerCollection: true` they are also published on `<prefix>.<collection>.CHANGED` (topic = entity id).
- With `collection` set, only that collection's events pass.
- `bus` may be `null` - then the bridge just exposes `cdc$`.
- `isConnected` turns `false` when the source completes or errors, or after `dispose()`.

`publishCdcToBus(bus, cdc$, options)` is the lower-level function that `createCdcBridge` uses; it returns a plain RxJS `Subscription`. `subscribeCdc(bus, options)` is its consumer-side counterpart: a cold `Observable` that registers a bus listener on subscribe and aborts it on unsubscribe.

## 3. Store Bridge (`attachStoreBridge`)

The store bridge is bidirectional: it does everything a CDC bridge does and additionally accepts mutation commands from the bus.

```typescript
import { createMsgBus } from '@actdim/msgmesh/core';
import { createLiveStruct } from '@actdim/livestruct';
import { attachStoreBridge } from '@actdim/msgmesh-store/bridge';

const bus = createMsgBus();
const store = await createLiveStruct({ name: 'workspace_db' });

const bridge = attachStoreBridge(bus, store, { channelPrefix: 'STORE' });

bridge.cdc$.subscribe((e) => console.log(e.origin, e.type, e.collection, e.id));
bridge.errors$.subscribe((err) => console.error(err.kind, err.error));

await bus.send({
    channel: 'STORE.COMMAND',
    group: 'in',
    topic: 'users',
    payload: { type: 'CREATE', id: 'u-100', delta: { name: 'Alice' } },
});

await bridge.whenIdle();
bridge.dispose();
```

### Command channels

The bridge listens (groups `in` and `out`, any topic) on:
- `<prefix>.COMMAND`
- `<prefix>.<boundCollection>.COMMAND` - only when the bridge is bound to a collection (through the `collection` option or because the target is a single collection).

### Command payload (`StoreCommandPayload`)

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `type` | `CREATE`, `PATCH`, `DELETE` or `PATCH_PATH`. `INSERT` / `UPDATE` are accepted as aliases. Deprecated alias field: `action`. |
| `id` | Document id (`docId` and `entityId` are also accepted). Required. |
| `collection` | Target collection. Optional, see resolution below. |
| `delta` | Fields to write. Deprecated alias: `data`. |
| `path`, `value` | For `PATCH_PATH`: dot path such as `settings.theme` and its new value. |
| `origin` | Origin recorded for the write (default `options.defaultOrigin`, then `bus`). |
| `mutationId` | Deduplication key. A fresh `crypto.randomUUID()` is generated when absent. |
| `correlationId` | Carried through to error events. |
| `durable` | When `true`, the target's `flush()` is awaited after the write. |
| `sourceId` | Commands carrying this bridge's own `sourceId` are ignored. |

`normalizeCommand` resolves the collection in this order: `payload.collection`; the segment before `COMMAND` in a channel like `STORE.users.COMMAND`; the message topic (unless it is a command verb or starts with `/`); the bound collection; `'default'`. The command type falls back to the message topic (for example topic `DELETE`) and finally to `PATCH`.

### Command semantics (`applyStoreCommand`)

| Type | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `CREATE` | Insert; if the document already exists, patch it instead (upsert). |
| `PATCH` | Patch if the document exists; otherwise insert the delta. |
| `PATCH_PATH` | Build a nested patch with `buildNestedPathPatch(path, value)` (for example `{ settings: { theme: 'dark' } }`), then patch-or-insert. |
| `DELETE` | Remove; a missing document or a failing remove is a silent no-op (`false`). |

### Origin filtering and republishing

Store CDC events are always emitted on `bridge.cdc$`. They are published to `<prefix>.ENTITY_CHANGED` only when:
1. the event was **not** produced by a bus command (its `mutationId` is not in the ledger), and
2. its origin is in `publishOrigins` (default `['local', 'remote']`).

Published events carry the bridge `sourceId`. Events produced by a bus command are re-labeled with the command origin (by default `bus`).

### Errors (`errors$`)

| `kind` | Raised when |
|---|---|
| `command` | The command targets a collection other than the bound one, there is no store target, or the store write throws. |
| `bus_send` | Publishing a CDC event to the bus fails. |
| `validation` | A command cannot be normalized (for example missing `id`), a CDC item is malformed, or the CDC source errors. |

## 4. Mutation Ledger (`MutationLedger`)

The ledger is the bridge's deterministic echo-suppression memory. It holds:
- `inFlight` - mutation ids currently being applied, with their origin;
- `applied` - completed mutation ids, bounded by `capacity` (default 4096) with oldest-first eviction.

```typescript
import { MutationLedger } from '@actdim/msgmesh-store';

const ledger = new MutationLedger(1024);
ledger.begin('m-1', 'bus');
ledger.isInFlight('m-1'); // true
ledger.markApplied('m-1');
ledger.end('m-1');
ledger.wasApplied('m-1'); // true
ledger.getInFlightOrigin('m-1'); // 'bus' (falls back to the applied origin)
```

The bridge skips a command whose `mutationId` is in flight or already applied (duplicate delivery), and treats a CDC event with such a `mutationId` as "via bus" (not republished).

> `EchoTracker` (time-window based) and the `echoSuppressionMs` option are deprecated. `attachStoreBridge` does not use them.

## 5. Keyed Serial Queue (`KeyedSerialQueue`)

```typescript
import { KeyedSerialQueue } from '@actdim/msgmesh-store';

const queue = new KeyedSerialQueue();
void queue.run('users:u-1', async () => save(1));
void queue.run('users:u-1', async () => save(2)); // runs after save(1)
void queue.run('users:u-2', async () => save(3)); // runs concurrently
await queue.drain();
```

- Tasks with the same key run one after another in FIFO order; different keys run concurrently.
- A rejected task does not reject later tasks for the same key.
- `size` is the number of keys with pending work; `drain()` waits until all of them settle.

Both the store bridge and the worker host use the key `<collection>:<id>`.

## 6. Mutation Targets

`resolveMutationTarget(store, { boundCollection })` turns a store into a `MutationTarget` (`get`, `insert`, `patch`, `remove`, optional `flush`). Recognized inputs, checked in order:

1. **Collection** - has `name`, `get`, `create`, `delete` (for example a LiveStruct `LiveCollection`). Bound to its `name`; writes use `engineAccess.commitRaw` when present so the `mutationId` is preserved.
2. **Store instance** - has `engine` with `insertDoc`, `patchDoc`, `deleteDoc`, `getDoc`.
3. **Low-level engine** - has `insertDoc`, `patchDoc`, `deleteDoc`, `getDoc` directly.
4. **Custom target** - already implements `get`, `insert`, `patch`, `remove`.

Anything else throws `UnsupportedStoreError`. With a bound collection, operations on another collection throw.

```typescript
import { attachStoreBridge, type StoreTarget } from '@actdim/msgmesh-store';

const memory = new Map<string, Record<string, unknown>>();
const target: StoreTarget = {
    get: async (c, id) => memory.get(`${c}:${id}`) ?? null,
    insert: async (c, id, data) => memory.set(`${c}:${id}`, data),
    patch: async (c, id, p) => memory.set(`${c}:${id}`, { ...memory.get(`${c}:${id}`), ...p }),
    remove: async (c, id) => memory.delete(`${c}:${id}`),
};

// A custom target has no CDC stream, so disable CDC.
const bridge = attachStoreBridge(bus, target, { enableCdcStream: false });
```

## 7. Worker Transport

### Ports (`WorkerMessagePortLike`)

Any object with `postMessage` plus one listener style (`addEventListener`, `on`, `addListener` or `onmessage`/`onerror`/`onclose` properties). `Worker`, `MessagePort`, a worker's `self` and Node `worker_threads` ports all fit; `addPortListener` / `removePortListener` pick the available style.

For tests, `createMessageChannelPair()` returns two connected `InMemoryMessagePort` instances. They clone every message with `structuredClone` (`safelyClone`) and deliver it in a microtask, just like a real port.

### Worker host (`attachWorkerStoreHost`)

Runs next to the store (inside the worker). It answers `INIT`, `COMMAND`, `QUERY` and `BATCH` requests, applies commands through the same `applyStoreCommand` used by the bridge, serializes them per `collection:docId`, and streams CDC back only while the client is subscribed - events produced in the same microtask are coalesced into one `CDC_BATCH` message.

The store may be passed directly or as a (possibly async) factory that is resolved on the first `INIT`. Stores whose engine `config` exists must have `forceMemory: true`; otherwise `WorkerHostStorageError` is thrown.

### Worker client (`createWorkerStoreClient`)

The main-thread facade:

```typescript
import { createMessageChannelPair, attachWorkerStoreHost, createWorkerStoreClient } from '@actdim/msgmesh-store/worker';

const { port1, port2 } = createMessageChannelPair();
const host = attachWorkerStoreHost(store, port1);
const client = createWorkerStoreClient(port2);

await client.ready();
const sub = client.cdc$.subscribe((e) => console.log('worker CDC', e.type, e.id));

await client.create('users', 'usr-1', { name: 'Alice' });
await client.patch('users', 'usr-1', { score: 10 });
await client.patchPath('users', 'usr-1', 'profile.bio', 'Hello');
const rows = await client.query('SELECT * FROM docs WHERE collection = ?', ['users']);
await client.delete('users', 'usr-1');

sub.unsubscribe();
client.dispose();
host.dispose();
```

- **States**: `idle` -> `initializing` -> `ready`; `dead` after a close or fatal error; `disposed` after `dispose()`.
- **`cdc$`** is refcounted: the first subscriber sends `CDC_SUBSCRIBE`, the last unsubscribe sends `CDC_UNSUBSCRIBE`.
- **`errors$`** receives `WorkerDeadError` on close or fatal errors, unsolicited host `ERROR` messages and `messageerror` events.
- **Batching**: `batch: 'microtask'` (or a custom scheduler function) groups requests issued in the same tick into a single `BATCH` message; each request still resolves or rejects individually.

---

## Document: docs/topic--03-architecture-and-wiring.md (Architecture & Wiring)

# Architecture & Wiring

[<- Back to 02. Core Concepts](./topic--02-core-concepts.md) | [Next: 04. Integration Guide ->](./topic--04-integration-guide.md)

---

## 1. Layers

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph Consumers
        UI["UI / toolbars<br/>(send commands)"]
        SVC["Decoupled services<br/>(audit, analytics, sync)"]
    end
    BUS["@actdim/msgmesh bus"]
    subgraph MS["@actdim/msgmesh-store"]
        BR["bridge: attachStoreBridge"]
        CDC["cdc: toStoreCdcObservable / createCdcBridge"]
        CORE["core: normalizeCommand, applyStoreCommand,<br/>MutationLedger, KeyedSerialQueue"]
        WK["worker: client / host / channel"]
    end
    STORE["@actdim/livestruct store / engine<br/>(or custom StoreTarget)"]

    UI -->|STORE.COMMAND| BUS
    BUS -->|STORE.ENTITY_CHANGED| SVC
    BUS <--> BR
    BR --> CORE
    BR --> CDC
    WK --> CORE
    WK --> CDC
    CORE -->|insert / patch / remove| STORE
    STORE -->|cdc$| CDC
```

- `core` has no knowledge of the bus or of workers. It normalizes commands, resolves store targets and applies mutations.
- `cdc` turns store streams into `StoreCdcEvent` and moves them to and from the bus.
- `bridge` composes `core` and `cdc` into a bidirectional bus attachment with echo suppression.
- `worker` composes `core` and `cdc` behind a `postMessage` protocol.

## 2. Command Path (bus -> store)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant P as Producer
    participant B as MsgMesh bus
    participant SB as Store bridge
    participant L as MutationLedger
    participant Q as KeyedSerialQueue
    participant S as Store

    P->>B: send STORE.COMMAND {type, id, delta, mutationId?}
    B->>SB: handleCommand(msg)
    SB->>SB: normalizeCommand (collection, type, mutationId)
    alt bound collection mismatch / no target / invalid
        SB-->>SB: errors$ (command | validation)
    else own sourceId or mutationId already seen
        SB-->>SB: ignore (duplicate / own echo)
    else accepted
        SB->>Q: run("collection:id")
        Q->>L: begin(mutationId, origin)
        Q->>S: applyStoreCommand (upsert / path patch / remove)
        Q->>L: markApplied + end
    end
```

Key properties:
- Commands for the same `collection:id` are applied in arrival order; other documents proceed in parallel.
- A command with a `mutationId` that is in flight or already applied is dropped, which makes redelivery idempotent.
- `durable: true` additionally awaits `flush()` on the target.

## 3. Change Path (store -> bus)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant S as Store cdc$
    participant SB as Store bridge
    participant L as MutationLedger
    participant C as bridge.cdc$
    participant B as MsgMesh bus

    S->>SB: raw change {type, collection, id, delta, mutationId}
    SB->>SB: normalize, clone, deep-freeze
    SB->>L: isInFlight / wasApplied(mutationId)?
    alt applied from a bus command (viaBus)
        SB->>C: emit with origin = command origin (default bus)
        Note over SB,B: not republished - echo suppressed
    else local or remote write
        SB->>C: emit with origin from event (default defaultOrigin)
        opt origin in publishOrigins
            SB->>B: STORE.ENTITY_CHANGED (group out, topic collection, + sourceId)
            opt secondaryChannelPerCollection
                SB->>B: STORE.{collection}.CHANGED (topic id)
            end
        end
    end
```

### Why the loop cannot form

1. A bus command is recorded in the ledger before the store write.
2. The store emits a CDC event with the same `mutationId`.
3. The bridge sees the id in the ledger and does not publish to the bus.
4. If another bridge forwards a published event back as a command with the original `sourceId`, the originating bridge ignores it.

Because the ledger is count-bounded (not time-bounded), suppression does not depend on timing; only ids older than the last `ledgerCapacity` applied mutations are forgotten.

## 4. Bus Topology

| Channel | Group | Topic | Direction | Producer |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<prefix>.COMMAND` | `in` or `out` | any (often the collection, or a command verb) | -> store | application |
| `<prefix>.<collection>.COMMAND` | `in` or `out` | any | -> store | application (bound bridges only) |
| `<prefix>.ENTITY_CHANGED` | `out` | collection | <- store | `attachStoreBridge`, `createCdcBridge`, `publishCdcToBus` |
| `<prefix>.<collection>.CHANGED` | `out` | entity id | <- store | same, with `secondaryChannelPerCollection` |

The default prefix is `STORE`. Several bridges with different prefixes can share one bus, for example one per bounded context.

## 5. Worker Topology

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph Main["Main thread"]
        APP["App code"]
        WC["createWorkerStoreClient"]
    end
    subgraph W["Web Worker"]
        WH["attachWorkerStoreHost"]
        Q2["KeyedSerialQueue"]
        ST["LiveStruct store<br/>(forceMemory: true)"]
    end
    APP -->|create / patch / patchPath / delete / query| WC
    WC -->|INIT, COMMAND, QUERY, BATCH,<br/>CDC_SUBSCRIBE, CDC_UNSUBSCRIBE, CLOSE| WH
    WH -->|INIT_OK, COMMAND_OK, QUERY_OK, BATCH_OK,<br/>CDC, CDC_BATCH, ERROR, CLOSE| WC
    WH --> Q2 --> ST
    ST -->|cdc$| WH
    WC -->|cdc$| APP
```

### Handshake and requests

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant H as Host
    participant S as Store

    C->>H: INIT {id, payload: initPayload}
    H->>S: resolve store (call factory once, retry up to factoryRetries)
    H-->>C: INIT_OK {ready: true}  (or ERROR)
    C->>H: CDC_SUBSCRIBE (first cdc$ subscriber)
    C->>H: COMMAND {type, collection, docId, delta | path+value, mutationId?}
    H->>S: applyStoreCommand (serialized per collection:docId)
    H-->>C: COMMAND_OK {mutationId}
    S-->>H: CDC events
    H-->>C: CDC (one event) or CDC_BATCH (same microtask)
    C->>H: CLOSE (client dispose)
```

Lifecycle rules enforced by the client:
- Every request has a timeout (`requestTimeoutMs`, default 10000; `initTimeoutMs`, default 5000).
- A `CLOSE` message or port `close` event marks the client `dead` and rejects all pending requests with `WorkerDeadError`.
- A port `error` event is fatal under `errorPolicy: 'fatal'` (default) and only reported on `errors$` under `'log'`.
- Requests are checked for cloneability before sending, so a non-cloneable payload rejects immediately instead of breaking the port.

### Batching

With `batch: 'microtask'`, requests issued in the same tick are queued and flushed once:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant H as Host
    C->>C: create(), patch(), query() in one tick
    C->>H: BATCH {payload: [COMMAND, COMMAND, QUERY]}
    H->>H: execute items (each isolated)
    H-->>C: BATCH_OK {results: [{id, success, result | error}]}
    C->>C: resolve / reject each original promise
```

A single queued request is sent unwrapped. `INIT` is never batched.

## 6. Combining Bridge and Worker

The two halves are independent. A common layout keeps the store in a worker and puts a bus on each side:

- Inside the worker, `attachStoreBridge(workerBus, store)` lets worker-side services exchange commands and CDC on a local bus.
- On the main thread, `createWorkerStoreClient(worker)` provides typed calls and `client.cdc$`; that stream can be forwarded to the main-thread bus with `publishCdcToBus(mainBus, client.cdc$)`.

See [04. Integration Guide](./topic--04-integration-guide.md) for runnable setups.

## Document: docs/topic--04-integration-guide.md (Integration Guide)

# Integration Guide

[<- Back to 03. Architecture & Wiring](./topic--03-architecture-and-wiring.md) | [Next: 05. API Reference ->](./topic--05-api-reference.md)

---

## 1. Installation

```bash
pnpm add @actdim/msgmesh-store @actdim/msgmesh @actdim/utico rxjs
# optional, when the target store is LiveStruct:
pnpm add @actdim/livestruct
```

### Peer dependencies

| Package | Range | Required | Used for |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rxjs` | `>=7.8.0` | yes | All streams (`cdc$`, `errors$`, operators). The only runtime import of this library. |
| `@actdim/msgmesh` | `>=1.12.0` | yes | The bus passed to `attachStoreBridge`, `createCdcBridge`, `publishCdcToBus`, `subscribeCdc`. |
| `@actdim/utico` | `>=1.12.0` | yes | Peer of `@actdim/msgmesh`. |
| `@actdim/livestruct` | `>=1.12.0` | optional | The typical store target. Any object matching `StoreTarget` works too. |

The library is ESM only (`"type": "module"`) and `sideEffects: false`. It uses `crypto.randomUUID()`, `structuredClone` and `queueMicrotask`, which are available in modern browsers, Web Workers and current Node LTS releases (global `crypto` requires Node 19 or later).

## 2. Bus + Store Bridge on One Thread

```typescript
import { createMsgBus } from '@actdim/msgmesh/core';
import { createLiveStruct } from '@actdim/livestruct';
import { attachStoreBridge, type StoreCdcEvent } from '@actdim/msgmesh-store';

const bus = createMsgBus();
const store = await createLiveStruct({ name: 'workspace_db' });

const bridge = attachStoreBridge(bus, store, {
    channelPrefix: 'STORE',
    publishOrigins: ['local', 'remote'], // default
});

// A decoupled service listens to published changes.
bus.on({
    channel: 'STORE.ENTITY_CHANGED',
    group: 'out',
    topic: '/.*/',
    callback: (msg) => {
        const event = msg.payload as StoreCdcEvent;
        console.log('changed', event.collection, event.id, event.origin);
    },
});

// Any module can write through the bus.
await bus.send({
    channel: 'STORE.COMMAND',
    group: 'in',
    topic: 'users',
    payload: { type: 'PATCH', id: 'u-1', delta: { role: 'admin' }, durable: true },
});

await bridge.whenIdle();
```

Direct writes (`(await store.collection('users')).create(...)`) are published with origin `local`; the `PATCH` sent above is applied but not republished, because it came from the bus.

### Binding a bridge to one collection

Pass a collection as the target, or set `collection`:

```typescript
const parts = await store.collection('parts');
const partsBridge = attachStoreBridge(bus, parts, { channelPrefix: 'PARTS' });

// Listens on PARTS.COMMAND and PARTS.parts.COMMAND
await bus.send({
    channel: 'PARTS.parts.COMMAND',
    group: 'in',
    topic: 'PATCH',
    payload: { id: 'part-101', delta: { color: 'green' } },
});
```

Commands that resolve to a different collection are rejected with an `errors$` event of kind `command`.

### Consuming CDC with filters

```typescript
import { subscribeCdc } from '@actdim/msgmesh-store/cdc';

const sub = subscribeCdc(bus, {
    channelPrefix: 'STORE',
    collection: 'orders',
    originFilter: ['local'],
    typeFilter: ['insert', 'update'],
}).subscribe((e) => audit(e));

// later
sub.unsubscribe(); // aborts the bus listener
```

### Publish-only setups

When you never accept bus commands, use `createCdcBridge` (or `attachStoreBridge` with `enableCommandHandling: false`):

```typescript
import { createCdcBridge } from '@actdim/msgmesh-store/cdc';

const cdcBridge = createCdcBridge(store, bus, {
    channelPrefix: 'STORE',
    secondaryChannelPerCollection: true,
    onError: (err) => console.error('CDC publish failed', err),
});
```

## 3. Store in a Web Worker

### Worker side

```typescript
// store.worker.ts
import { createLiveStruct } from '@actdim/livestruct';
import { attachWorkerStoreHost, type WorkerMessagePortLike } from '@actdim/msgmesh-store/worker';

attachWorkerStoreHost(
    () => createLiveStruct({ name: 'workspace_db', forceMemory: true }),
    self as unknown as WorkerMessagePortLike,
    { factoryRetries: 1 }
);
```

- The factory runs on the first `INIT`; concurrent `INIT`s share one promise. After `factoryRetries + 1` failed attempts the host fails permanently.
- A store whose engine `config.forceMemory` is not `true` throws `WorkerHostStorageError` - a persistent engine must not be hosted by this transport.
- Raw `query()` calls are forwarded to `engine.queryRaw(sql, params, options.collection)` (or `store.query(sql, params)`).

### Main-thread side

```typescript
import { createWorkerStoreClient, type WorkerMessagePortLike } from '@actdim/msgmesh-store/worker';

const worker = new Worker(new URL('./store.worker.ts', import.meta.url), { type: 'module' });
const client = createWorkerStoreClient(worker as unknown as WorkerMessagePortLike, {
    initTimeoutMs: 5000,
    requestTimeoutMs: 10000,
    errorPolicy: 'fatal',
});

client.errors$.subscribe((err) => console.error('worker store', err));
client.cdc$.subscribe((e) => console.log('CDC', e.type, e.collection, e.id));

await client.ready();
await client.create('users', 'u-1', { name: 'Alice' });
await client.patchPath('users', 'u-1', 'settings.theme', 'dark');
```

The casts are needed only because DOM typings declare `onmessage` with `MessageEvent`; the runtime objects satisfy `WorkerMessagePortLike`.

### Lifecycle and recovery

```typescript
import { WorkerDeadError } from '@actdim/msgmesh-store/worker';

try {
    await client.patch('users', 'u-1', { score: 1 });
} catch (err) {
    if (err instanceof WorkerDeadError) {
        const next = new Worker(new URL('./store.worker.ts', import.meta.url), { type: 'module' });
        await client.reconnect(next as unknown as WorkerMessagePortLike);
    }
}

// On shutdown: sends CLOSE, rejects pending calls, terminates the worker
// (set terminateOnDispose: false to keep the port open).
client.dispose();
```

### Forwarding worker CDC to a main-thread bus

```typescript
import { publishCdcToBus } from '@actdim/msgmesh-store/cdc';

const forward = publishCdcToBus(mainBus, client.cdc$, { channelPrefix: 'STORE' });
// forward.unsubscribe() stops forwarding and releases the CDC subscription
```

## 4. Batching Option

Bursts of small requests can be sent as one `postMessage`:

```typescript
const client = createWorkerStoreClient(port, { batch: 'microtask' });

await Promise.all([
    client.create('users', 'u-1', { name: 'A' }),
    client.create('users', 'u-2', { name: 'B' }),
    client.query('SELECT * FROM docs WHERE collection = ?', ['users']),
]); // one BATCH message, one BATCH_OK reply
```

| `batch` value | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `'none'` or omitted | Each request is posted immediately. |
| `'microtask'` | Requests made in the same tick are flushed together in a microtask. |
| `(flush) => void` | Custom scheduler; call `flush()` when the batch should be sent, for example `(flush) => requestAnimationFrame(flush)`. |

Each item in a batch succeeds or fails independently. If the whole `BATCH` fails with an `ERROR`, every item in it is rejected.

## 5. Testing Without a Browser

```typescript
import { createLiveStruct } from '@actdim/livestruct';
import { createMessageChannelPair, attachWorkerStoreHost, createWorkerStoreClient } from '@actdim/msgmesh-store/worker';

const store = await createLiveStruct({ name: 'test', forceMemory: true });
const { port1, port2 } = createMessageChannelPair();
const host = attachWorkerStoreHost(store, port1);
const client = createWorkerStoreClient(port2);

await client.ready();
// ... assertions ...
client.dispose();
host.dispose();
await store.close();
```

For bridge tests, `await bridge.whenIdle()` after sending commands instead of waiting on timers. A mock bus only needs `send` (returning a promise) and `on`.

## 6. Checklist

- Choose one `channelPrefix` per bridge and keep it consistent between producers and consumers.
- Supply a stable `mutationId` when a command may be redelivered; the bridge then applies it once.
- Subscribe to `errors$` on both bridges and worker clients - failures are reported there, not thrown.
- Always `dispose()` bridges, CDC bridges, worker clients and hosts; disposal aborts bus listeners and completes streams.

## Document: docs/topic--05-api-reference.md (API Reference)

# API Reference

[<- Back to 04. Integration Guide](./topic--04-integration-guide.md) | [Back to Main README](../README.md)

---

All exports are available from the root entry `@actdim/msgmesh-store`. The subpath entries `./bridge`, `./cdc` and `./worker` expose the subsets listed below. The `core` module (section 4) is exported only from the root entry, except `buildNestedPathPatch`, which `./worker` re-exports.

## 1. `@actdim/msgmesh-store/bridge`

### `attachStoreBridge(bus, storeOrCollection, options?)`

```typescript
function attachStoreBridge(
    bus: MsgMeshBusLike,
    storeOrCollection: StoreTarget | null,
    options?: StoreBridgeOptions
): StoreBridgeController;
```

Attaches a store to a bus: listens for commands on `<prefix>.COMMAND` (and `<prefix>.<collection>.COMMAND` when bound), applies them per document in order, emits store CDC on `cdc$` and publishes non-bus changes on `<prefix>.ENTITY_CHANGED`. Throws `UnsupportedStoreError` when the store cannot be resolved. With `null` the bridge has no CDC and reports every command as an error.

### `StoreBridgeOptions`

| Option | Type | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `channelPrefix` | `string` | `'STORE'` | Prefix of all channels. |
| `enableCdcStream` | `boolean` | `true` | Subscribe to the store CDC stream. Disable for targets without CDC. |
| `enableCommandHandling` | `boolean` | `true` | Register bus command listeners. |
| `defaultOrigin` | `StoreCdcOrigin` | `'local'` for CDC | Origin for CDC events without one; also the command origin fallback (else `'bus'`). |
| `collection` | `string` | target's collection | Bind the bridge to one collection. |
| `secondaryChannelPerCollection` | `boolean` | `false` | Also publish on `<prefix>.<collection>.CHANGED`. |
| `publishOrigins` | `StoreCdcOrigin[]` | `['local', 'remote']` | Origins that are published to the bus. |
| `freezeEvents` | `boolean` | `true` | Clone and deep-freeze CDC events. |
| `ledgerCapacity` | `number` | `4096` | Capacity of the internal `MutationLedger`. |
| `onInvalid` | `(error, rawItem) => void` | - | Called for malformed CDC items (also reported on `errors$`). |
| `echoSuppressionMs` | `number` | - | Deprecated, ignored. |

### `StoreBridgeController`

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `isConnected: boolean` | `true` until disposed or the CDC source completes or errors. |
| `isDisposed: boolean` | `true` after `dispose()`. |
| `cdc$: Observable<StoreCdcEvent>` | All store changes, labeled with origin. Throws when the bridge has no store. |
| `errors$: Observable<BridgeErrorEvent>` | Command, bus send and validation errors. |
| `whenIdle(): Promise<void>` | Resolves when all queued commands have settled. |
| `dispose(): void` | Aborts listeners, unsubscribes CDC, completes streams. Idempotent. |
| `disconnect(): void` | Deprecated alias of `dispose()`. |

### Types

- **`StoreCommandType`** - `'CREATE' | 'PATCH' | 'DELETE' | 'PATCH_PATH'`.
- **`StoreCommandPayload<T>`** - `{ type?, action? (deprecated), collection?, id, delta?, data? (deprecated), path?, value?, origin?, correlationId?, mutationId?, durable?, sourceId? }`.
- **`BridgeErrorEvent`** - union of:
  - `BridgeCommandErrorEvent` - `{ kind: 'command', collection?, id?, mutationId?, correlationId?, error }`
  - `BridgeBusSendErrorEvent` - `{ kind: 'bus_send', channel?, topic?, error }`
  - `BridgeValidationErrorEvent` - `{ kind: 'validation', error }`

### `EchoTracker` (deprecated)

```typescript
class EchoTracker {
    constructor(ttlMs?: number); // default 1000
    record(mutationId: string, origin?: StoreCdcOrigin, extra?: { collection?: string; id?: string }): void;
    isEcho(mutationId: string, expectedOrigin?: StoreCdcOrigin): boolean;
    has(mutationId: string): boolean;
    getOrigin(mutationId: string): StoreCdcOrigin | undefined;
    prune(now?: number): void;
    clear(): void;
    readonly size: number;
    dispose(): void;
}
```

Sliding time-window tracker kept for backwards compatibility; `EchoRecord` is its record type. Use `MutationLedger` instead.

## 2. `@actdim/msgmesh-store/cdc`

### Types

- **`StoreCdcType`** - `'insert' | 'update' | 'delete'`.
- **`StoreCdcOrigin`** - `'local' | 'remote' | 'bus'`.
- **`StoreCdcEvent<T>`** - `{ type, collection, id, delta, origin, timestamp, mutationId?, sourceId? }` (all readonly).
- **`CdcSubscriptionOptions`** - `{ channelPrefix?, collection?, id?, originFilter?, typeFilter? }`.
- **`CdcBridgeOptions`** - `{ channelPrefix?, defaultOrigin?, collection?, secondaryChannelPerCollection?, onError?, onInvalid?, freezeEvents? }`.
- **`CdcBridge`** - `{ isDisposed, isConnected, cdc$, dispose(), disconnect() (deprecated) }`.
- **`MsgMeshBusLike`** - `{ send(params): Promise<unknown>; on?(params: MsgMeshBusOnParams): (() => void) | void }`; a real `createMsgBus()` instance satisfies it.
- **`MsgMeshBusOnParams`** - `{ channel, group?, topic?, callback?, handler?, ... }`.
- **`ToStoreCdcObservableOptions`** - `{ defaultCollection?, defaultOrigin?, onInvalid?, freezeEvents? }`.

### Functions

| Function | Signature | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `toStoreCdcObservable` | `(source: unknown, options?: ToStoreCdcObservableOptions) => Observable<StoreCdcEvent>` | Normalize an observable, store, engine, engine access or collection into CDC events. Throws when no stream can be found. |
| `filterCdc` | `(options?: CdcSubscriptionOptions) => MonoTypeOperatorFunction<StoreCdcEvent>` | Filter by collection, id, origins and types. |
| `filterCollection` | `(collection: string) => MonoTypeOperatorFunction<StoreCdcEvent>` | Shorthand for `filterCdc({ collection })`. |
| `filterEntity` | `(collection: string, id: string) => MonoTypeOperatorFunction<StoreCdcEvent>` | Shorthand for `filterCdc({ collection, id })`. |
| `publishCdcToBus` | `(bus: MsgMeshBusLike, cdc$: Observable<StoreCdcEvent>, options?: CdcBridgeOptions) => Subscription` | Publish each event on `<prefix>.ENTITY_CHANGED` (and optionally the per-collection channel). |
| `subscribeCdc` | `(bus: MsgMeshBusLike, options?: CdcSubscriptionOptions) => Observable<StoreCdcEvent>` | Cold observable of bus CDC events with filtering; unsubscribing aborts the listener. |
| `createCdcBridge` | `(source: unknown, bus?: MsgMeshBusLike \| null, options?: CdcBridgeOptions) => CdcBridge` | Disposable source-to-bus publisher. |
| `deepFreeze` | `<T>(obj: T, visited?: Set<unknown>) => T` | Recursively freeze an object in place (cycle safe). |
| `safeClone` | `<T>(val: T) => T` | `structuredClone`, falling back to JSON, then a shallow copy. |
| `safeSend` | `(bus, params, onError?) => Promise<unknown>` | Call `bus.send` and route any sync or async failure to `onError`; never rejects. |

## 3. `@actdim/msgmesh-store/worker`

### Client

```typescript
function createWorkerStoreClient(
    portOrWorker: WorkerMessagePortLike,
    options?: WorkerStoreClientOptions
): WorkerStoreClient;
```

**`WorkerStoreClientOptions`** (alias `WorkerClientOptions`):

| Option | Type | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `initTimeoutMs` | `number` | `5000` | Timeout of the `INIT` handshake. |
| `requestTimeoutMs` | `number` | `10000` | Timeout of every other request. |
| `autoInit` | `boolean` | `true` | Start the handshake immediately. |
| `initPayload` | `Record<string, unknown>` | - | Sent as `INIT.payload`. |
| `terminateOnDispose` | `boolean` | `true` | Call `terminate()` (or `close()`) on the port in `dispose()`. |
| `errorPolicy` | `'fatal' \| 'log'` | `'fatal'` | Whether a port `error` event kills the client. |
| `batch` | `'none' \| 'microtask' \| ((flush) => void)` | none | Request batching. |

**`WorkerStoreClient`**:

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `state: WorkerClientState` | `'idle' \| 'initializing' \| 'ready' \| 'dead' \| 'disposed'`. |
| `isReady`, `isDisposed` | State shortcuts. |
| `cdc$: Observable<StoreCdcEvent>` | Refcounted CDC stream from the host. |
| `errors$: Observable<unknown>` | `WorkerDeadError`, unsolicited host errors, `messageerror`. |
| `ready(): Promise<void>` | Run or await the handshake. |
| `reconnect(port?): Promise<void>` | Reset to `idle`, optionally swap the port, resubscribe CDC and handshake again. |
| `create(collection, id, data, options?)` | `CREATE` command; `options.mutationId` optional. |
| `patch(collection, id, delta, options?)` | `PATCH` command. |
| `patchPath(collection, id, path, value, options?)` | `PATCH_PATH` command. |
| `delete(collection, id, options?)` | `DELETE` command. |
| `query<T>(sql, params?): Promise<T[]>` | Raw SQL query in the worker. |
| `dispose()` | Reject pending calls, send `CLOSE`, detach listeners, complete streams, terminate the port. |
| `disconnect?()` | Deprecated alias of `dispose()`. |

### Host

```typescript
function attachWorkerStoreHost(
    storeOrFactory: StoreOrFactory,
    portOrSelf: WorkerMessagePortLike,
    options?: WorkerHostOptions
): WorkerHostController;

function validateStoreForWorker(store: unknown): void;
```

- **`StoreOrFactory`** - a store, or `() => store | Promise<store>`.
- **`WorkerHostOptions`** - `{ defaultOrigin? (default 'local'), collection?, factoryRetries? (default 1) }`.
- **`WorkerHostController`** - `{ isDisposed, store (resolved store or null), dispose() }`. `dispose()` sends `CLOSE`, stops CDC and calls the store's `close()` or `dispose()`.
- **`validateStoreForWorker`** - throws `WorkerHostStorageError` when the store or its engine has a `config` without `forceMemory: true`.

### Channel utilities

| Export | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `safelyClone<T>(data: T): T` | `structuredClone` without fallback; throws `DataCloneError` for non-cloneable data. |
| `addPortListener(port, type, listener)` | Register via `addEventListener`, `on`, `addListener` or `on<type>` property. |
| `removePortListener(port, type, listener)` | Counterpart of `addPortListener`. |
| `InMemoryMessagePort` | In-memory port with microtask delivery; extra members `isClosed`, `triggerError(error)`, `close()`, `terminate()`. |
| `createMessageChannelPair(): { port1, port2 }` | Two connected `InMemoryMessagePort` instances. |
| `buildNestedPathPatch` | Re-export of the core helper. |

### Errors

- **`WorkerDeadError`** - operation on a dead or disposed client; also used to reject pending requests.
- **`WorkerHostStorageError`** - non in-memory store hosted in the worker.

### Wire protocol types

| Type | Shape |
|---|---|
| `WorkerRequestAction` | `'CREATE' \| 'PATCH' \| 'PATCH_PATH' \| 'DELETE'` |
| `WorkerRequestType` | `'INIT' \| 'COMMAND' \| 'QUERY' \| 'BATCH' \| 'CDC_SUBSCRIBE' \| 'CDC_UNSUBSCRIBE' \| 'CLOSE'` |
| `WorkerInitRequest` | `{ id, type: 'INIT', payload?: { storeName?, options?, ... } }` |
| `WorkerCommandRequest` | `{ id, type: 'COMMAND', payload: { type?, action?, collection, docId, delta?, data?, path?, value?, mutationId? } }` |
| `WorkerQueryRequest` | `{ id, type: 'QUERY', payload: { sql, params? } }` |
| `WorkerBatchRequest` | `{ id, type: 'BATCH', payload: WorkerClientRequest[] }` |
| `WorkerCdcSubscribeMessage` / `WorkerCdcUnsubscribeMessage` | `{ type: 'CDC_SUBSCRIBE' }` / `{ type: 'CDC_UNSUBSCRIBE' }` |
| `WorkerCloseMessage` | `{ type: 'CLOSE', reason? }` (both directions) |
| `WorkerClientRequest` | Union of all client-to-host messages. |
| `WorkerInitResponse` | `{ id, type: 'INIT_OK', payload? }` |
| `WorkerCommandResponse` | `{ id, type: 'COMMAND_OK', payload?: { mutationId?, ... } }` |
| `WorkerQueryResponse` | `{ id, type: 'QUERY_OK', payload: { rows } }` |
| `WorkerBatchResultItem` | `{ id, success, result?, error? }` |
| `WorkerBatchResponse` | `{ id, type: 'BATCH_OK', payload: { results } }` |
| `WorkerCdcResponse` | `{ type: 'CDC', payload: StoreCdcEvent }` |
| `WorkerCdcBatchMessage` | `{ type: 'CDC_BATCH', payload: StoreCdcEvent[] }` |
| `WorkerErrorResponse` | `{ id?, type: 'ERROR', error: { message, name?, stack?, code? } }` |
| `WorkerHostMessage` | Union of all host-to-client messages. |
| `WorkerMessageEventLike<T>` | `{ data: T }` |
| `WorkerMessagePortLike` | `postMessage` plus optional listener methods, `onmessage`/`onerror`/`onclose`, `terminate`, `close`, `start`. |

## 4. Core (root entry only)

### `MutationLedger`

```typescript
class MutationLedger {
    constructor(capacity?: number); // default 4096
    readonly capacity: number;
    readonly inFlight: Map<string, string>;
    readonly applied: Map<string, number>;
    begin(mutationId: string, origin: string): void;
    end(mutationId: string): void;
    isInFlight(mutationId: string): boolean;
    getInFlightOrigin(mutationId: string): string | undefined;
    markApplied(mutationId: string, origin?: string): void;
    wasApplied(mutationId: string): boolean;
    clear(): void;
}
```

### `KeyedSerialQueue`

```typescript
class KeyedSerialQueue {
    readonly size: number;
    run<T>(key: string, task: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T>;
    drain(): Promise<void>;
}
```

### Command and target functions

| Export | Signature | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `normalizeCommand` | `(msg: unknown, defaults?: NormalizeCommandDefaults) => NormalizedStoreCommand` | Parse a bus message or raw payload; throws on missing `id` or non-object input. |
| `resolveMutationTarget` | `(store: unknown, options?: { boundCollection?: string }) => MutationTarget` | Adapt a collection, store instance, engine or custom target. |
| `applyStoreCommand` | `(target: MutationTarget, cmd: NormalizedStoreCommand) => Promise<unknown>` | Execute upsert / path patch / delete semantics; flush when `durable`. |
| `buildNestedPathPatch` | `(path: string, value: unknown) => Record<string, unknown>` | `'a.b.c', 1` -> `{ a: { b: { c: 1 } } }`. |
| `UnsupportedStoreError` | `class extends Error` | Thrown by `resolveMutationTarget`. |

### Types

- **`NormalizedStoreCommand`** - `{ type, collection, id, delta?, path?, value?, mutationId, correlationId?, origin, durable?, sourceId?, rawPayload? }`.
- **`NormalizeCommandDefaults`** - `{ defaultCollection?, defaultOrigin?, boundCollection? }`.
- **`MutationTarget`** - `{ boundCollection?, get, insert, patch, remove, flush? }` with `(collection, id, ..., mutationId?, origin?)` parameters.
- **`StoreTarget`** - `LiveStoreTarget | LiveEngineTarget | LiveCollectionTarget | CustomStoreTarget`.
- **`LiveEngineTarget`** - `getDoc`, `insertDoc`, `patchDoc`, `deleteDoc`, optional `flush` (LiveStruct engine shape).
- **`LiveCollectionTarget`** - `name`, `get`, `create`, `delete`, optional `flush` (LiveStruct collection shape).
- **`LiveStoreTarget`** - `engine: LiveEngineTarget`, optional `collection(name)`, optional `flush`.
- **`CustomStoreTarget`** - either `{ get, insert?, patch?, remove?, flush? }` with `(collection, id, ...)` methods, or `{ collection(name), flush? }`. Note: `resolveMutationTarget` (and therefore `attachStoreBridge`) only accepts the first form with all four methods present; the `collection(name)` form is resolved only inside `attachWorkerStoreHost`.
